_comment: The words on each game's start page (wordlink.au/<slug>). tools/build-links.py reads this and writes the pages. name is the H1 and the game's name; seo is the <title>; meta is the search snippet; sub is the one line a learner reads; about, how, cls and good are the part below Play, written for teachers and tutors. Keep every page's text its own: search engines ignore a paragraph repeated across pages.

games.name: Letter Names
games.seo: Letter Names Game: Hear an English Letter and Tap It | Free Alphabet Practice for Adults
games.meta: Free alphabet game for adult English learners. Hear a letter name, tap the right letter. Printed and handwritten letters. No sign-up.
games.sub: Hear a letter name and choose the letter.
games.blurb: Hear a letter name and tap it from four. Every third round shows the letters handwritten, so learners recognise both styles.
games.about: An alphabet listening game for adults learning English letters for the first time. The learner hears a letter name, like "G" or "J", and taps it from four letters. Some rounds show the letters handwritten instead of printed, so learners recognise both.
games.cls: Open the Teacher Game, choose Letter Names, and students join on their phones with the room code or QR code. The projector says the letter and everyone answers at once.
inside: All 26 letters of the alphabet, A to Z, shown as capital letters.
Each round says one letter name and shows four letters to choose from.
Every third round shows the four letters handwritten instead of printed, so learners meet both styles.
tips: Many learners know a letter's sound before its name, or the other way round. Letter names are what a learner needs to spell their name aloud on the phone or at a counter.
After the game, practise letters with similar names aloud in pairs, such as B and P, D and T, G and J, or M and N.
Play [Big and Small Letters](big-and-small-letters) next, so each name links to both the capital and the small form.

games.name: Big and Small Letters
games.seo: Big and Small Letters: Match Capital and Lowercase Letters | Free Game for Adult Learners
games.meta: Match uppercase and lowercase letters, then write names with a capital letter. Free English literacy game for adults.
games.sub: Match big and small letters.
games.blurb: Find the small partner of a capital letter, or the capital of a small one. Writing rounds turn a name like fatima into Fatima.
games.about: A matching game for uppercase and lowercase letters. The learner sees a capital letter and finds its small letter, or the other way round. Other rounds show a name in small letters, like "fatima", and ask the learner to write it with a capital at the start.
how: Tap its big or small partner.
In writing rounds, type the name with a capital letter.
games.cls: Choose Big and Small Letters in the Teacher Game. Students tap on their phones while the letter shows on the projector.
inside: Two kinds of round, taking turns: matching a letter to its other form, and writing a name with a capital.
Matching rounds show one letter, capital or small, and four letters to choose from. Any of the 26 letters can come up.
Writing rounds use common names: Ali, Fatima, Nada, Hassan, Maria, Omar, Linh and Sara.
In the writing rounds the capital is checked, so fatima is marked wrong and Fatima is marked right.
tips: Letters whose small form looks different from the capital, like A and a, D and d, G and g, Q and q, and R and r, need the most practice.
b, d, p and q are the same shape turned around. Practise them side by side on paper.
Follow with [Trace Your Name](trace-your-name), so learners write their own name with a capital at the start.

games.name: Beginner Sound Gap
games.seo: Beginner Sound Gap: CVC Word Families Phonics Game | Free Phonics for Adult Beginners
games.meta: Phonics game with CVC word families like -at, -an, -ig and -ot. Hear the word, tap the missing first sound. Free for adult learners.
games.sub: Hear the missing sound and tap it.
games.blurb: Hear a short word like cat and tap the missing first sound in _at. Each round stays in one rhyming family, from -an to -un.
games.about: A first phonics game built on short CVC word families: -an, -at, -ap, -et, -en, -ig, -in, -ip, -op, -ot, -ug and -un. The learner hears a word like "cat", sees "_at" and taps the missing first sound. Every round stays in one rhyming family, so one sound decides the answer.
how: Look at the word with a gap.
games.cls: Choose Beginner Sound Gap in the Teacher Game. The projector shows the word family and students tap the sound on their phones.
inside: 12 short vowel word families: -an, -at, -ap, -et, -en, -ig, -in, -ip, -op, -ot, -ug and -un.
Everyday three-letter words such as man, cat, map, pet, pen, pig, pin, zip, mop, hot, bug and sun.
Each round shows the word with its first letter missing, like ?at, and four first letters to choose from.
All four choices make a real word in the same family, so the learner has to listen for the first sound.
Two to four words from one family come in a row before the game moves on, so the rhyme is easy to hear.
tips: Say the word slowly with the class and stretch the first sound: mmm, an, man.
Many languages do not separate the short vowels of English. Say pairs like pin and pen, or cat and cut, aloud and let learners hear the difference.
Next, [Beginner Tap Word](beginner-tap-word) asks learners to read the whole word.

games.name: Beginner Tap Word
games.seo: Beginner Tap Word: Read CVC Rhyming Words | Free Decoding Game for Adult Learners
games.meta: Hear a short word and tap it from rhyming words like cat, bat, hat. A free decoding game for adults learning to read English.
games.sub: Hear a word and tap it.
games.blurb: Hear a word like pen and pick it from pen, hen, ten and men. Only the first sound changes, so the learner must read it.
games.about: A decoding game with short rhyming words. The learner hears "pen" and chooses from pen, hen, ten and men. The words differ by one sound, so the learner has to read the first letter, not guess. It uses the same word families as Beginner Sound Gap.
games.cls: Choose Beginner Tap Word in the Teacher Game. The word is spoken from the projector and students tap it on their phones.
inside: The same 12 short vowel families as [Beginner Sound Gap](beginner-sound-gap), from -an to -un.
Each round says one word and shows four words from its family, like pen, hen, ten and men.
Only the first letter changes, so the learner has to look at the start of the word.
Two to four words from one family come in a row before the game moves on.
tips: Ask learners to point to the first letter of each word before they tap.
When a learner taps the wrong rhyme, say both words aloud and compare only the first sounds.
Next, [Beginner Build Word](beginner-build-word) asks learners to spell the word from its sounds.

games.name: Beginner Build Word
games.seo: Beginner Build Word: Build CVC Words From Sounds | Free Blending Game for Adults
games.meta: Put the sounds in order to build short words like man, pig and sun. Free phonics blending and segmenting game for adult learners.
games.sub: Build the word from its sounds.
games.blurb: Put sound tiles in order to spell a word you hear, like m, a, n for man. Every tile plays its own sound in a real voice.
games.about: A blending and segmenting game. The learner hears a short word and puts its sound tiles in order, like m, a, n for "man". Each tile plays its sound, recorded by a real voice. It is the step from hearing sounds to spelling words.
how: Tap or drag the sound tiles into order.
games.cls: Choose Beginner Build Word in the Teacher Game. Students build the word on their phones and the answers show on the projector.
inside: Words from the same 12 short vowel families, each made of three sounds: m, a, n for man, or s, u, n for sun.
The sound tiles are mixed up, and the learner puts them in order to build the word they heard.
Two to four words from one family come in a row, so only the first sound changes from word to word.
tips: Model it aloud: say the word, then each sound, then the word again. Man. M, a, n. Man.
Ask learners to write the word on paper after they build it.
Once these words are easy, move to [Elementary Build Word](elementary-build-word), where two letters can make one sound.

games.name: Elementary Sound Gap
games.seo: Elementary Sound Gap: Digraphs and Vowel Teams Phonics Game | sh, ch, th, ee, ai, oa
games.meta: Phonics game for digraphs and vowel teams: sh, ch, th, wh, ph, ee, ea, ai, ay, oa, oo, ou. Hear the word, tap the missing sound.
games.sub: Hear the missing sound in a longer word.
games.blurb: Tap the missing two-letter sound in everyday words like ship, phone and train. Covers sh, ch, th and vowel teams such as ee, ai and oa.
games.about: The next step in phonics, built on two-letter sounds: consonant digraphs (sh, ch, th, wh, ph) and vowel teams (ee, ea, ai, ay, oa, oe, ie, ue, oo, ou and more). The learner hears a word like "rain" and taps the missing sound. The words are from everyday life: ship, chips, phone, train, boat.
games.cls: Choose Elementary Sound Gap in the Teacher Game. It is a good way to revise one sound pattern with the whole class.
good: long vowel sounds ee ai oa
inside: Consonant pairs: sh, ch, th, wh and ph, in words like ship, chips, this, think, when and phone.
Vowel pairs: ee, ea, ai, ay, oa, oe, ie, ue, oo, ou, ow, oi, oy, au and aw, in words like tree, eat, rain, day, boat, pie, blue, moon, book, out, cow, coin, boy and saw.
Silent e words, like cake, nine, hope, ride and game.
Beginning blends: st, bl, tr, dr, cl, fl, gr, pl, br, cr, sl and sp, in words like stop, black, tree, class, green and play.
Common endings: ck, ll, ff, ss, zz, tch, dge, ed and ing, in words like duck, ball, catch, bridge, played and going.
The wrong choices are other patterns from the same group, so sh is set against patterns like ch, th, wh and ph.
tips: Teach one group at a time, starting with the consonant pairs, before mixing them in the game.
oo and ou each make more than one sound: moon and book, out and could. Point this out before those rounds.
Use the study lists in [Words 2](words-2) on the home page to hear each pattern before playing.

games.name: Elementary Tap Word
games.seo: Elementary Tap Word: Read Words With Digraphs and Vowel Teams | Free Game for Adults
games.meta: Hear a word and tap it from words with the same sound pattern, like boat, coat, road. Free English decoding game for adults.
games.sub: Hear a longer word and tap it.
games.blurb: Hear a word and choose it from four with the same pattern, like moon, food, soon and pool. Reading the whole word is the only way to be sure.
games.about: A decoding game for words with digraphs and vowel teams. The four choices share a sound pattern, like moon, food, soon and pool, so the learner has to read the whole word.
games.cls: Choose Elementary Tap Word in the Teacher Game and students answer on their phones.
inside: The same patterns as [Elementary Sound Gap](elementary-sound-gap): consonant pairs, vowel pairs, silent e, beginning blends and common endings.
Each round says one word and shows four words that share its pattern, like moon, food, soon and pool, or catch, match, watch and pitch.
Because the choices share a pattern, the learner has to read the rest of the word to find the right one.
tips: Ask learners to find the shared pattern first, then look at what is different in each word.
Some families are sight words as much as sound words, like could, would and should. Say them together as a set.
Next, [Elementary Build Word](elementary-build-word) asks learners to spell these words from their sounds.

games.name: Elementary Build Word
games.seo: Elementary Build Word: Build Words From Sound Tiles (Graphemes) | Free Phonics for Adults
games.meta: Build words like ship, train and moon from grapheme tiles, where two letters can make one sound. Free phonics game for adults.
games.sub: Build a longer word from its sounds.
games.blurb: Build words from tiles where two letters make one sound: ship is sh, i, p and train is t, r, ai, n. A key step towards spelling longer words.
games.about: The learner builds words from sound tiles, not single letters: "ship" is sh, i, p and "train" is t, r, ai, n. It teaches that two letters can make one sound, which is the key to spelling longer English words.
how: Put the sound tiles in order.
games.cls: Choose Elementary Build Word in the Teacher Game. The projector shows everyone's answers, so mistakes are easy to talk about.
inside: Words from the same patterns as [Elementary Sound Gap](elementary-sound-gap), built from sound tiles rather than single letters.
A pair of letters that makes one sound stays on one tile: ship is sh, i, p, train is t, r, ai, n, and catch is c, a, tch.
In silent e words the e has its own tile at the end, like c, a, k, e for cake.
Longer words come up too, like jumped, playing and bridge.
tips: Before playing, ask learners how many sounds they hear in a word like ship. The answer is three, even though it has four letters.
Talk through mistakes on the projector. A learner who looks for an s tile and an h tile in ship is reading letters, not sounds.
Ask learners to write the word on paper after they build it.

games.name: Sight Words
games.seo: Sight Words Game: Hear and Tap Common English Words | Free High-Frequency Words for Adults
games.meta: Hear a common word like the, was, have or would, and tap it. A free sight words and high-frequency words game for adults.
games.sub: The words you see everywhere.
games.blurb: Hear a common word like the, was or come and tap it from four. Many of these words cannot be sounded out, so they need to be known on sight.
games.about: A game for high-frequency sight words like the, and, you, was, have, come, would and little. Many of them cannot be sounded out, so learners need to know them by sight. The learner hears the word and taps it from four written words.
games.cls: Choose Sight Words in the Teacher Game for a quick warm-up.
inside: 30 high-frequency words: the, and, you, was, they, said, with, what, from, there, were, this, that, some, here, your, then, been, which, their, into, more, than, many, down, would, have, little, come and when.
Each round says one word and shows four written words to choose from.
tips: Point out the pairs that look alike, such as then and than, there and their, and were and where.
Ask learners to find these words in a short text you are reading in class. They are in almost every sentence.
Use [Test Yourself: Reading](test-reading) to see which of them a learner already knows.

games.name: Picture and Word
games.seo: Picture and Word: Match a Picture to Its English Word | Free Reading Game for Adults
games.meta: Look at a picture and tap its word. A free vocabulary and early reading game for adult English learners. No typing.
games.sub: Look at the picture and tap its word.
games.blurb: Look at a picture, such as a bus or an apple, and tap its word from four. The instruction is spoken and there is no typing.
games.about: An early reading game where a picture carries the meaning. The learner sees a picture, like a bus or an apple, and taps its word from four written words. There is no typing, and the instruction is spoken.
how: Tap the word for the picture.
games.cls: Choose Picture and Word in the Teacher Game. The picture shows on the projector and students tap the word on their phones.
inside: 18 everyday words, each with a clear picture: bus, train, apple, banana, egg, fish, rice, phone, door, book, pen, bag, bed, key, chair, shoe, clock and soap.
The instruction is spoken. The four word choices are not, so the learner has to read them.
There is no typing: the learner taps the word.
tips: Hold up the real objects in class, like a pen, a key or a book, and ask learners to find the word.
Learners who find this easy can move to [Copy It](copy-it), which uses many of the same words.

games.name: Read the Notice
games.seo: Read the Notice: Find the Date, Time and Price on a Notice | Free Reading Practice for Adults
games.meta: Read short notices like a class time, a shop closure or a bus timetable. Find what, when and how much. Free survival English reading.
games.sub: Find what a notice tells you.
games.blurb: Read a short notice, like a shop closed sign or a bus timetable, and answer what, when or how much. Practises finding the key detail.
games.about: A reading game with short everyday notices: an English class, a shop closed sign, a bus timetable, a doctor's appointment and a for sale sign. The learner answers one question: what is it about, when is it, or how much is it. It practises scanning for the key information.
games.cls: Choose Read the Notice in the Teacher Game, then ask the class where they see notices like these.
inside: Five notices: an English class (Room 4, Monday 9:00 am, Free), Shop Closed (back Tuesday), a bus timetable (Stop 12, every 20 minutes, $3.50), a doctor (Clinic Road, Friday 2:30 pm, $40.00) and a For Sale sign.
Each round asks one question: what is this notice about, when is it, or how much is it.
The choices are the other lines of the same notice, so the learner has to know which line answers which question.
tips: Bring in real notices from your centre or a local shop, and ask the same three questions.
Point out where a notice usually puts each thing: the heading at the top, then the place, the time and the price.
For more everyday reading, try [Messages](messages) and [Read the List](read-the-list).

games.name: Copy It
games.seo: Copy It: Copy Words, Names and Numbers | Free Writing and Typing Practice for Adults
games.meta: Copy a word, a full name or a number exactly, with capitals in the right place. Free copying practice for adult literacy learners.
games.sub: Copy a word, a name or a number.
games.blurb: Copy a word, a full name like Mai Nguyen, or a number. Capitals have to match, the same way a form expects a name to be written.
games.about: Copying practice for learners starting to write. Rounds take turns between a word (some with a picture), a full name like "Mai Nguyen" and a number. Capital letters must match, so learners practise writing names the way forms expect them.
how: Look at the word, name or number.
games.cls: Choose Copy It in the Teacher Game. It works well before a paper form activity.
inside: Three kinds of round, taking turns: a word, a full name and a number.
The words are everyday ones like bus, shop, milk, home, work, door, bank, rent, open, stop and exit. Ten of them have a picture beside the word.
The names are Ali Hassan, Mai Nguyen, Fatima Ahmadi and Chen Wei, and need a capital at the start of each name and a space between them.
The numbers go from 1 to 99.
A copy with the right letters but the wrong capitals scores part marks.
tips: Ask learners to copy the same words on paper as well. Typing is not the same skill as writing with a pen.
Use the name rounds to talk about first name and family name, then move to [Forms](forms).
For handwriting, use [Trace the Letters](trace-letters) and [Trace Your Name](trace-your-name).

games.name: Capitals and Full Stops
games.seo: Capitals and Full Stops: Punctuation Game for Adult English Learners | Free
games.meta: Choose the correctly written sentence, or add the capital letter and full stop. Free punctuation practice for adults.
games.sub: Start big, end with a full stop.
games.blurb: Choose the sentence that is written correctly, or rewrite one with a capital letter and a full stop. Everyday sentences like I live in Springvale.
games.about: A punctuation game for the first two rules: a sentence starts with a capital letter and ends with a full stop. Some rounds ask which of four sentences is written correctly. Others give a sentence in small letters to write again properly. The sentences are about everyday life, like "I live in Springvale."
how: Tap the right one, or write it correctly.
games.cls: Choose Capitals and Full Stops in the Teacher Game and go through the wrong answers together.
good: capital letters and full stops activity
inside: Two kinds of round, taking turns: choose the correct sentence, and rewrite a sentence correctly.
In the choosing rounds, one sentence is correct, one has no capital, one has no full stop, and one has neither.
In the writing rounds, the sentence is shown in small letters with no full stop, and the learner writes it with both.
The sentences are about everyday life: name, family, home, daily routine and the weekend, like I live in Springvale or I take the bus to class.
tips: Some sentences also have a name or a place, like Springvale or Vietnam. Use these to show that names take a capital too.
After the game, ask learners to write one sentence about themselves with a capital and a full stop.
Next, [Write a Sentence](write-a-sentence) asks learners to write two sentences of their own.

games.name: Write a Sentence
games.seo: Write a Sentence About Yourself: Model Sentences for Adult English Learners | Free
games.meta: Follow a model like "My name is David. I am from Vietnam." and write two sentences about yourself. Free writing practice for adults.
games.sub: Write a sentence about you.
games.blurb: Follow two model sentences to write two of your own, about your name, country, home, family or work. The capital letters and full stops are checked too.
games.about: Guided writing from a model. The learner sees two model sentences, like "My name is David. I am from Vietnam.", and writes two sentences about themselves the same way. Topics are name and country, where you live, family, class day, language and work. Capitals and full stops count.
how: Change them to be about you.
games.cls: Choose Write a Sentence in the Teacher Game. Students' sentences show on the projector, which is a good start for speaking.
inside: Six models, each two short sentences: My name is David. I am from Vietnam. / I live in Springvale. I have two children. / My class is on Monday. I come by bus. / My name is Sara. I speak Arabic. / I have three children. They go to school. / I work in a shop. I start at nine.
The learner writes two sentences about themselves that follow the model.
Copying the model back word for word earns part marks only, because the sentences should be about the learner.
Each sentence is checked for a capital letter at the start and a full stop at the end. In the name and country model, the name and the country need capitals too.
tips: Read the model aloud first and ask a learner to say their own version before anyone writes.
Put the answers on the projector and read some aloud together. It leads straight into speaking practice.
Learners who are not ready for this can start with [Capitals and Full Stops](capitals-and-full-stops).

games.name: All Spelling
games.seo: All Spelling: Hear and Spell English Words From Every Topic | Free Spelling Game for Adults
games.meta: Mixed spelling game: numbers, days, months, weather, fruit, body and clothes words. Type it or choose it. Free for adult English learners.
games.sub: Spell words from every topic.
games.blurb: A mixed spelling round from every topic: number words, days, months, weather, fruit, body and clothes. Multiple choice makes it easier.
games.about: A mixed spelling review across the vocabulary topics: number words, days, months, weather, fruit, parts of the body and clothes. The learner hears a word and types it. Multiple choice is there for an easier round.
games.cls: Choose All Spelling in the Teacher Game for an end-of-week spelling quiz.
inside: Every word from the vocabulary games in one mix: number words one to ten, days of the week, months, weather, fruit, parts of the body and clothes.
The learner hears a word and types it. Multiple choice is off at the start and can be switched on for an easier game.
A Hint button sounds the word out, then shows it one part at a time.
When a word is wrong, the learner sees their spelling under the right one, part by part, and can tap each part to hear its sound.
tips: Use it at the end of a week as a review of the topics you covered.
For one topic at a time, play [Days of the Week](days), [Months](months), [Weather](weather), [Fruits](fruits), [Parts of the Body](body) or [Clothes](clothes).

games.name: Days of the Week
games.seo: Days of the Week Game: Hear and Spell Monday to Sunday | Free English for Adults
games.meta: Hear a day of the week and spell it, with a capital letter. Free English vocabulary and spelling game for adult learners.
games.sub: Hear a day of the week and write it.
games.blurb: Hear a day of the week and type it, capital letter included. Learners who cannot type yet can tap instead.
games.about: A listening and spelling game for the seven days, Monday to Sunday. Days start with a capital letter and the game marks that, so learners learn to write them properly. Multiple choice is there for learners who cannot type yet.
how: Type it with a capital letter.
games.cls: Choose Days of the Week in the Teacher Game, then ask "What day is today?"
inside: The seven days, Monday to Sunday.
The learner hears a day and types it. A Hint button sounds the word out, then shows it one part at a time.
A day spelled correctly without its capital scores part marks, because days always take a capital in English.
Multiple choice is on at the start, for learners who cannot type yet. Switch it off for a spelling game.
tips: Wednesday, Thursday and Saturday are the hardest to spell. Say Wed-nes-day slowly, the way it is written, to help learners remember the letters.
Start each lesson by asking what day it is today, and what day it was yesterday.
Next, play [Months](months), then [Find the Date](find-the-date) to read days on a calendar.

games.name: Months
games.seo: Months of the Year Game: Hear and Spell January to December | Free English for Adults
games.meta: Hear a month and spell it, with a capital letter. Free months of the year spelling game for adult English learners.
games.sub: Hear a month and write it.
games.blurb: Hear a month and type it with a capital letter. February, August and September usually need the most practice.
games.about: A listening and spelling game for the twelve months. Learners hear the month and type it with its capital letter. February, August and September are the usual hard ones.
how: Type it with a capital letter.
games.cls: Choose Months in the Teacher Game, then follow up with Find the Date.
inside: The twelve months, January to December.
The learner hears a month and types it. A Hint button sounds the word out, then shows it one part at a time.
A month spelled correctly without its capital scores part marks.
Multiple choice is on at the start and can be switched off for a spelling game.
tips: February, August and September cause the most mistakes. February has an r that many people do not say.
Ask each learner to say and write the month of their birthday.
Follow with [Find the Date](find-the-date) and [Ordinal Numbers](ordinal-numbers), which practise saying dates.

games.name: Weather
games.seo: Weather Words Game: Sunny, Rainy, Windy, Humid | Free English Vocabulary for Adults
games.meta: Hear and spell weather words: sunny, cloudy, rainy, windy, stormy, foggy, hot, cold, warm, humid. Free ESL game for adults.
games.sub: Hear a weather word and write it.
games.blurb: Hear and spell words like sunny, windy, cold and humid, or tap the matching picture. Words for small talk and the weather forecast.
games.about: Vocabulary and spelling for the weather: sunny, cloudy, rainy, windy, snowy, stormy, foggy, hot, cold, warm, cool and humid. These are the words for small talk and for reading a weather forecast. In multiple choice the learner taps the matching picture.
how: Type it, or tap the picture.
games.cls: Choose Weather in the Teacher Game, then ask "What is the weather like today?"
inside: 12 weather words: sunny, cloudy, rainy, windy, snowy, stormy, foggy, hot, cold, warm, cool and humid.
The learner hears a word and types it, or in multiple choice taps the matching picture.
Multiple choice is on at the start. Switch it off for a spelling game.
tips: Point out the pattern in sunny, cloudy, rainy, windy, snowy, stormy and foggy: a weather word with y on the end.
Look at today's weather forecast on the projector and ask learners to find the words.
Pair it with [Clothes](clothes): It is cold. Wear a jumper.

games.name: Fruits
games.seo: Fruit Names Game: Hear and Spell Fruits in English | Free Vocabulary for Adult Learners
games.meta: Apple, banana, mango, watermelon and more. Hear a fruit name and spell it, or tap its picture. Free English game for adults.
games.sub: Hear the fruit and write its name.
games.blurb: Hear and spell fruit names from apple to watermelon, or tap the picture in multiple choice. Handy words for the shops.
games.about: Fruit vocabulary for shopping: apple, banana, orange, grape, mango, peach, plum, pear, lemon, cherry, strawberry, watermelon, pineapple, coconut and kiwi. The learner hears the word and spells it, or in multiple choice taps the matching picture.
how: Type it, or tap the picture.
games.cls: Choose Fruits in the Teacher Game, and follow up with Shop or Read the List.
inside: 15 fruits: apple, banana, orange, grape, mango, peach, plum, pear, lemon, cherry, strawberry, watermelon, pineapple, coconut and kiwi.
The learner hears a word and types it, or in multiple choice taps the matching picture.
Multiple choice is on at the start. Switch it off for a spelling game.
tips: Strawberry, watermelon and pineapple are two words joined together. Splitting them, straw and berry, makes them easier to spell.
Bring in a supermarket catalogue and ask learners to find the fruit and its price.
Follow with [Shop](shop) or [Read the List](read-the-list) for prices and money.

games.name: Parts of the Body
games.seo: Parts of the Body Game: Head, Knee, Wrist, Stomach | Free English for the Doctor
games.meta: Hear and spell 24 parts of the body, from head to toe. Free English vocabulary for adults, useful at the doctor or chemist.
games.sub: Hear a part of the body and write it.
games.blurb: Hear and spell body words from head to toe, with clear drawings. The words for telling a doctor where it hurts.
games.about: Body vocabulary with clear drawings: head, eye, ear, nose, mouth, tooth, tongue, neck, shoulder, arm, elbow, wrist, hand, finger, thumb, chest, stomach, back, hip, leg, knee, ankle, foot and toe. These are the words for telling a doctor where it hurts.
how: Type it, or tap the picture.
games.cls: Choose Parts of the Body in the Teacher Game, then practise "My ... hurts."
good: parts of the body for adults
inside: 24 body words: head, eye, ear, nose, mouth, tooth, tongue, neck, shoulder, arm, elbow, wrist, hand, finger, thumb, chest, stomach, back, hip, leg, knee, ankle, foot and toe.
Each word has a clear drawing. In multiple choice the learner taps the matching picture.
Multiple choice is on at the start. Switch it off for a spelling game.
tips: Some of these words have letters you do not hear, like the k in knee, the w in wrist and the b in thumb. Point these out before a spelling game.
Practise the sentence for the doctor: My knee hurts. My back hurts.
Teach the plurals that change, too: one tooth, two teeth, and one foot, two feet.

games.name: Clothes
games.seo: Clothes Vocabulary Game: Jumper, Thongs, Beanie, Hoodie | Free Australian English for Adults
games.meta: Hear and spell 34 clothing words, including Australian ones like jumper, thongs and singlet. Free ESL vocabulary for adults.
games.sub: Hear the clothing word and write it.
games.blurb: Hear and spell clothes and accessories, with drawings. Includes Australian words like jumper, thongs and beanie.
games.about: Clothes and accessories with drawings, including Australian English words: shirt, jumper, jacket, coat, pants, jeans, shorts, singlet, hoodie, socks, shoes, boots, sandals, thongs, hat, cap, beanie, helmet, scarf, gloves, belt, glasses, watch, wallet, backpack, umbrella and more.
how: Type it, or tap the picture.
games.cls: Choose Clothes in the Teacher Game, then pair it with Weather: "It is cold. Wear a jumper."
inside: 34 words for clothes and accessories, including shirt, jumper, jacket, dress, pants, jeans, singlet, hoodie, socks, boots, thongs, beanie, helmet, scarf, gloves, glasses, watch, wallet, backpack and umbrella.
Australian English is used throughout: jumper rather than sweater, pants rather than trousers, and thongs for the footwear.
The learner hears a word and types it, or in multiple choice taps the matching picture.
tips: Thongs means footwear in Australia. Learners may know a different meaning from other English, so it is worth a quick explanation.
Ask learners to describe what they are wearing today: I am wearing a jumper and jeans.
Pair it with [Weather](weather): It is raining. Take an umbrella.

games.name: Odd One Out
games.seo: Odd One Out Picture Game: Find the One That Does Not Belong | Free English for Adults
games.meta: Four pictures, three belong together. Animals, fruit, transport, clothes, food, weather, colours and more. Free ESL game for adults.
games.sub: Find the word that does not belong.
games.blurb: Look at four pictures and tap the one that is not from the same group, like animals, transport or clothes. Builds vocabulary by meaning.
games.about: A picture game for grouping words by meaning. The learner sees four pictures, three from one group (animals, fruit, transport, clothes, body, food, weather, colours, numbers or actions), and taps the one that is different. It builds vocabulary in categories.
how: Find the one that is different.
games.cls: Choose Odd One Out in the Teacher Game, then ask students to say why.
inside: Ten groups: animals, fruit, transport, clothes, the body, food, weather, colours, numbers and actions.
Each round shows three pictures from one group and one from another group. The learner taps the one that does not belong.
Groups that overlap are never mixed. For example, fruit is never set against food, so there is only ever one right answer.
tips: After each round, ask learners to say why: The bus is not an animal.
Ask learners to name the group as well as the odd one out. It builds the words for categories, like transport and clothes.
Use [Test Yourself: Vocabulary](test-vocabulary) to see which topics a learner already knows.

games.name: Beginner Listen and Fill Gaps
games.seo: Beginner Listening Game: Hear a Sentence and Fill the Gap | Free English for Adults
games.meta: Hear simple sentences about you, like "I live in Springvale.", and write the missing word. Free listening practice for adults.
games.sub: Listen to a sentence and fill the gaps.
games.blurb: Hear a short sentence about someone, like My ___ is David, and type or tap the missing word. The sentence can be played again.
games.about: A listening gap-fill with short personal sentences, like "My ___ is David.", "I am ___ Vietnam." and "I go to English ___ three days a week." The learner hears the whole sentence and types the missing word, or taps it in multiple choice. The audio can be played again.
how: Type or tap the missing word.
games.cls: Choose Beginner Listen and Fill Gaps in the Teacher Game. The projector reads the sentence aloud to the whole room.
inside: 30 short sentences about one person, David, and his life: name, country, home, family, class, daily routine and the weekend.
Examples: My ___ is David. I am ___ Vietnam. I ___ two children. I take the ___ to class. I ___ up at 7:00.
The missing words are everyday ones like name, from, live, have, am, are, bus, family and went.
The learner hears the whole sentence and types the missing word, or taps it in multiple choice.
tips: Ask learners to say the whole sentence aloud after each round, with their own details: My name is Amina.
Many gaps are small grammar words like am, are and have. These are hard to hear in fast speech, so replay the sentence and listen for them.
When this is easy, move to [Elementary Listen and Fill Gaps](elementary-listening).

games.name: Elementary Listen and Fill Gaps
games.seo: Elementary Listening Game: Fill the Gap in Longer Sentences | Free English for Adults
games.meta: Hear longer everyday sentences and write the missing word. Free listening and gap-fill practice for adult English learners.
games.sub: Listen to a longer sentence and fill the gaps.
games.blurb: Hear a longer sentence and fill the gap. The sentences use the elementary sound patterns, so listening supports phonics.
games.about: A listening gap-fill with longer sentences, like "She ___ at the fish shop on the main street." The sentences use the Elementary sound patterns (sh, ee, oo, ai), so listening and phonics go together. The learner types the missing word, or taps it in multiple choice.
how: Type or tap the missing word.
games.cls: Choose Elementary Listen and Fill Gaps in the Teacher Game.
inside: 12 longer sentences built on the elementary sound patterns, like She ___ at the fish shop on the main street, and I ___ the train to the city on weekdays.
The missing words are mostly verbs: shops, eat, took, ride, stop, picked, eats, opens, walk and catch.
The learner types the missing word, or taps it in multiple choice.
tips: Listen for the s at the end of a verb, as in she eats and he opens. Learners often miss it when listening and leave it off when writing.
Ask learners to find the sound patterns in each sentence, such as sh in fish and ee in green.
Practise the patterns themselves with [Elementary Sound Gap](elementary-sound-gap).

games.name: Listen and Unscramble
games.seo: Listen and Unscramble: Hear a Sentence, Put the Words in Order | Free Game for Adults
games.meta: Hear a sentence, then drag the word tiles into order. Sentences about name, family, home and daily routine. Free ESL game.
games.sub: Listen, then put the words in order.
games.blurb: Hear a sentence about family, home or the weekend, then put the word tiles in order. In multiple choice, tap the correct sentence.
games.about: A listening and word order game. The learner hears a sentence, like "I have one son and one daughter.", then puts the mixed-up word tiles in order. The sentences cover personal information, family, home, daily routine and the weekend. In multiple choice the learner taps the sentence in the right order.
how: Tap or drag the words into order.
games.cls: Choose Listen and Unscramble in the Teacher Game.
inside: 76 sentences about one person's life: name and age, country, family, home, daily routine, the weekend, likes and what he can do.
Examples: I have one son and one daughter. I take the bus to class. I went to the park with my children. I want to find a good job.
The learner hears the sentence, then puts the word tiles in order. In multiple choice they tap the sentence in the right order.
tips: Ask learners to read the finished sentence aloud, then change one detail to make it true for them.
Point out the pattern most sentences follow: who, then the action, then the rest. I take the bus to class.
For the same sentences without audio, play [Grammar Unscramble](word-order).

games.name: Greetings
games.seo: Greetings Game: Hello, How Are You, Thank You | Free English Listening for Adult Beginners
games.meta: Hear a greeting or a question like "Where are you from?" and tap the right reply. Free everyday English for adults.
games.sub: Hear a greeting and answer it.
games.blurb: Hear a greeting or a simple question, like How are you? or Where are you from?, and tap the right reply. Social English for the first weeks.
games.about: Everyday exchanges for the first weeks of English. The learner hears a greeting or courtesy phrase, like "How are you?", "Thank you." or "See you next week.", and taps the right reply. Other rounds ask short personal questions: "What is your name?", "Where are you from?", "How old are you?"
how: Listen to what the person says.
games.cls: Choose Greetings in the Teacher Game, then have students say the replies to each other.
inside: Two kinds of round, taking turns: greetings and courtesy phrases, and short personal questions.
Greetings: Hello, Good morning, How are you?, Thank you, Sorry!, Please sit down, I am going home now, and See you next week.
Questions: What is your name?, Where are you from?, How old are you?, Where do you live?, Do you have children? and What is your phone number?
The replies are short, like Fine, thanks or You're welcome, and each reply can be heard as well as read.
tips: After the game, practise the same exchanges in pairs, standing up, as if meeting at the door.
Talk about which replies fit which situation. Goodbye and Bye can both end a conversation, but Good night is only for the evening.
For longer answers to questions, play the [Speaking Game](speaking-game).

games.name: Do What It Says
games.seo: Do What It Says: Follow Simple Spoken Instructions | Free English Listening for Adults
games.meta: Hear "Tap the book", "Open the door" or "Turn the sound off" and tap the right picture. Free listening game for adults.
games.sub: Listen, then tap what it says.
games.blurb: Hear a short instruction, like Open the door or Take a photo, and tap the matching picture. Covers classroom and phone instructions.
games.about: A game for following short spoken instructions. Classroom rounds use everyday things: "Tap the book.", "Open the door.", "Tap the cup." Device rounds use phone instructions: "Turn the sound off.", "Charge the battery.", "Take a photo." Every answer has a picture.
games.cls: Choose Do What It Says in the Teacher Game, then do the same instructions for real in the room.
inside: Two kinds of instruction: classroom ones, and turning things on and off on a phone.
Classroom: tap the book, the pen, the bag, the chair, the cup or the window, and open the door.
Phone: turn the sound on or off, turn on the internet, charge the battery, take a photo, and put it in the bin.
The learner hears the instruction and taps the matching picture from four.
tips: Do the classroom instructions for real after the game: open the door, point to a chair.
Then do the phone instructions on learners' own phones, such as turning the sound off before class.
For more phone skills, try [Screen Symbols](screen-symbols) and [What Should You Do?](what-should-you-do).

games.name: Speaking Game
games.seo: Speaking Practice Game: Answer Everyday Questions in English | Free for Adult Learners
games.meta: Hear a question like "What did you do on Saturday?" and build the answer from word tiles. Free English speaking preparation for adults.
games.sub: Hear the question and build your answer.
games.blurb: Hear a question like Where do you live? and build the answer from word tiles. The answer is then read aloud so the learner can say it too.
games.about: Practice for common conversation questions. The learner hears a question, like "Where do you live?", "What is your favourite food?", "Can you drive?" or "How was your weekend?", and builds a full answer from word tiles, like "On Saturday, I stayed at home." The answer is read aloud afterwards so the learner can say it too. In multiple choice the learner taps the right answer instead. To record their own voice, learners can use Speaking Practice on the home page.
how: Put the word tiles in order to make the answer.
Hear the answer and say it.
games.cls: Choose Speaking Game in the Teacher Game, then ask each student the same question aloud.
inside: 57 everyday questions in 13 topics: greetings, name, country, class, home, family, a partner, days, time, daily routine, the weekend, likes and things you can do.
Examples: Where do you live? How many children do you have? What time do you wake up? What did you do on Saturday? Can you drive?
The model answers are short sentences from one person, David, like I live in Springvale or On Saturday, I stayed at home.
Questions about the day, like What day is today?, are answered with the real day.
tips: After building David's answer, ask the learner to say their own answer aloud.
Put learners in pairs to ask each other the same questions after the game.
To record their own voice and compare it with a model, learners can use [Speaking Practice](speaking) on the home page.

games.name: Question Words
games.seo: Question Words Game: What, Where, How, Who | Free English Grammar for Adults
games.meta: Choose the right question word for everyday questions like "___ old are you?" and "___ do you live?". Free ESL grammar game.
games.sub: Choose the right question word.
games.blurb: Read a question with its first word missing, like ___ is your name?, and choose the question word. The questions asked at enrolment, the doctor and work.
games.about: A reading game for question words. The learner sees an everyday question with its first word missing, like "___ is your name?" or "___ do you spell your name?", and taps or writes the right question word. These are the questions asked at enrolment, at the doctor and at work.
games.cls: Choose Question Words in the Teacher Game, then have pairs ask each other the questions.
inside: 58 everyday questions with the first word missing. Most start with a question word: what, where, when, who, why or how.
Some start with do, are or can, like Do you have children? and Can you drive?
The three wrong choices are chosen so that only one word fits each question.
In multiple choice the learner reads the question and taps the word. In the typing game they hear the question and type the missing word.
tips: Teach the meaning of each question word with a simple answer: where is a place, when is a time, who is a person.
How many and what time come up often. Practise them as fixed phrases.
After the game, learners ask each other the questions in pairs, or use the [Speaking Game](speaking-game).

games.name: Grammar Unscramble
games.seo: Grammar Unscramble: Put English Words in the Right Order | Free Sentence Game for Adults
games.meta: Drag the word tiles into a correct sentence, like "I live in a three-bedroom house." Free English word order practice for adults.
games.sub: Put the words in the right order.
games.blurb: Put the mixed-up words of a written sentence in order, with no audio. The sentences are about yourself, your family and your day.
games.about: A word order game with no audio. The learner sees the words of a sentence mixed up and puts them in order. The sentences are about personal information, family, home and daily routine, so they are useful for speaking and writing about yourself.
how: Tap or drag them into order.
games.cls: Choose Grammar Unscramble in the Teacher Game.
inside: The same 76 sentences as Listen and Unscramble, about name, family, home, daily routine and the weekend.
There is no audio. The learner reads the mixed-up words and puts them in order.
In multiple choice the learner taps the sentence in the right order instead.
tips: The capital letter on the first word and the full stop on the last are clues. Point them out.
Ask learners to read the finished sentence aloud, then write it on paper.
For the same sentences with audio, play [Listen and Unscramble](unscramble).

games.name: Translate
games.seo: Translate to English: Arabic, Dari, Persian, Pashto, Vietnamese, Chinese and More | Free
games.meta: Read a sentence in your language and write it in English. Arabic, Burmese, Chinese, Dari, Hindi, Khmer, Pashto, Persian, Thai, Urdu, Vietnamese.
games.sub: Read it in your language, write it in English.
games.blurb: Read a sentence in your first language, such as Arabic, Dari or Vietnamese, and write it in English. For learners who can read their own language.
games.about: A translation game for learners who can read their first language. The learner reads a sentence in Arabic, Burmese, Chinese, Dari, Hindi, Khmer, Pashto, Persian, Thai, Urdu or Vietnamese and writes it in English. In multiple choice they choose the right English sentence. The sentences are about name, family, home, daily routine and the weekend.
how: Write it in English, or tap it.
games.cls: Choose Translate in the Teacher Game. Each student picks their own language on their phone.
inside: 79 sentences about name, age, country, family, home, daily routine and the weekend, like My name is David and I am from Vietnam.
Eleven languages: Arabic, Burmese, Chinese, Dari, Hindi, Khmer, Pashto, Persian, Thai, Urdu and Vietnamese.
The learner reads the sentence in their language and writes it in English, or taps the right English sentence in multiple choice.
A Hint button shows the English sentence one word at a time.
tips: This game is for learners who can read their first language. For learners who cannot, use the listening and picture games instead.
In a mixed class, each learner chooses their own language, so the whole class can play together.
Ask learners to say the English sentence aloud after writing it.

games.name: Numbers 1 to 10
games.seo: Number Words 1 to 10: Hear and Spell One to Ten | Free English Numbers for Adults
games.meta: Hear a number and spell its word: one, two, three... ten. Type it or choose it. Free English number words game for adults.
games.sub: Hear a number from 1 to 10 and spell it.
games.blurb: Hear a number from one to ten and type its word. Learners who cannot type yet can tap instead.
games.about: A spelling game for the number words one to ten. The learner hears the number and types the word, like "seven" or "eight". Multiple choice is there for learners who cannot type yet.
games.cls: Choose Numbers 1 to 10 in the Teacher Game.
inside: The number words one to ten.
The learner hears a number and types its word. Multiple choice is on at the start, for learners who cannot type yet.
A Hint button sounds the word out, then shows it one part at a time.
tips: Two, four and eight have letters that are hard to hear, like the w in two and the gh in eight. Point these out before a spelling game.
Write the digit beside the word on the board: 8, eight. Many learners know the digit long before the word.
Next, play [Numbers 11 to 20](numbers-11-20).

games.name: Numbers 11 to 20
games.seo: Number Words 11 to 20: Thirteen or Thirty? | Free English Numbers Game for Adults
games.meta: Hear and spell eleven to twenty, the hardest English numbers to hear and spell. Free number words game for adult learners.
games.sub: Hear a number from 11 to 20 and spell it.
games.blurb: Hear a number from eleven to twenty and type its word. The teen numbers, like twelve, fifteen and eighteen, are the hard ones.
games.about: A spelling game for eleven to twenty. The teen numbers are hard to hear and hard to spell: twelve, fifteen, eighteen. The learner hears the number and types the word.
games.cls: Choose Numbers 11 to 20 in the Teacher Game, and point out the stress in thirTEEN and THIRty.
inside: The number words eleven to twenty.
The learner hears a number and types its word. Multiple choice is on at the start.
tips: Say thirteen and thirty side by side, and stress the end: thirTEEN, THIRty. Learners mix these up when listening to prices and times.
Eleven and twelve do not follow the teen pattern. Teach them on their own first.
Next, play [Numbers 21 to 99](numbers-21-99).

games.name: Numbers 21 to 99
games.seo: Number Words 21 to 99: Hear and Spell Twenty-One to Ninety-Nine | Free for Adults
games.meta: Hear a number and spell it, like forty-two or ninety-nine. Free English number words game for adult learners.
games.sub: Hear a number from 21 to 99 and spell it.
games.blurb: Hear a number like forty-two and spell it. Needed for writing amounts in words.
games.about: A spelling game for two-digit number words, like twenty-one, forty-two and ninety-nine. Learners practise the tens words they need for forms and for writing amounts in words. The hyphen is shown as the standard form, and a space is accepted too.
games.cls: Choose Numbers 21 to 99 in the Teacher Game.
inside: The number words from twenty-one to ninety-nine.
The learner hears a number and types its word. The hyphen is the standard way to write it, but twenty one with a space is also accepted.
Multiple choice is on at the start.
tips: Teach the tens words first: twenty, thirty, forty, fifty. Forty has no u, which surprises many learners.
Then show that the rest is a tens word and a ones word joined: forty and two make forty-two.
For writing numbers in figures instead of words, play [Write the Number](write-the-number).

games.name: Tap the Number
games.seo: Tap the Number: Hear a Number and Find It | Free Number Recognition Game for Adults
games.meta: Hear a number from 0 to 10 and tap it from four. Free number recognition game for adult learners, with no typing.
games.sub: Hear a number and tap it.
games.blurb: Hear a number from 0 to 10 and tap it from four. The wrong choices are close, so it trains careful listening with no typing.
games.about: A number recognition game with no typing. The learner hears a number from 0 to 10 and taps it from four numbers. The wrong choices include the numbers on either side, so the learner has to listen carefully.
games.cls: Choose Tap the Number in the Teacher Game as a quick warm-up.
inside: Numbers from 0 to 10, including zero.
The learner hears a number and taps it from four. The wrong choices include the numbers either side, like 6 and 8 for 7.
There is no typing, so learners who cannot type yet can play.
tips: Zero is often skipped in class, but it is in every phone number. Practise saying zero and oh.
Say a number and ask learners to hold up that many fingers, then find it in the game.
Next, play [Write the Number](write-the-number), where learners write the digits themselves.

games.name: Write the Number
games.seo: Write the Number: Write Numbers and Australian Money in Figures | Free for Adults
games.meta: Hear a number or price and write it in figures, or write what an Australian coin or note is worth. Free numeracy for adults.
games.sub: Write numbers and money in figures.
games.blurb: Write numbers and money in figures: a number from 0 to 10, the value of a $1, $2, $5 or $10, or an amount like $7.
games.about: Writing numbers and money in figures. Rounds mix three kinds: write a number from 0 to 10 that you hear or see, write what an Australian coin or note is worth ($1, $2, $5 or $10), and write a whole dollar amount up to $10, like $7.
how: Listen, or look at the coin or note.
games.cls: Choose Write the Number in the Teacher Game.
inside: Three kinds of round, mixed: a number, a coin or note, and an amount of money.
Numbers from 0 to 10, either heard or shown to copy.
Coins and notes: a picture of a $1, $2, $5 or $10, and the learner writes what it is worth.
Money amounts in whole dollars up to $10, like $7, either heard or shown to copy.
tips: Bring real coins and notes to class and ask learners to write what each one is worth.
Show that $5 and $5.00 are the same amount. The game accepts both.
For bigger amounts and cents, play [Shop](shop) and [Read the List](read-the-list).

games.name: Add It Up
games.seo: Add It Up: Simple Addition in English | Free Numeracy Game for Adult Learners
games.meta: Hear and read a simple sum like 4 + 3, then type the answer. Free numeracy and maths English for adults.
games.sub: Add two numbers together.
games.blurb: Hear and read a simple sum, like four plus three, and type the answer. The maths stays easy so the English is the focus.
games.about: Simple addition, asked in English. The sum is spoken ("What is four plus three?") and shown on screen. The maths is easy on purpose: the aim is understanding numbers and "plus" in English.
games.cls: Choose Add It Up in the Teacher Game.
inside: Two numbers that add up to 10 or less, like 4 + 3.
The sum is spoken, What is four plus three?, and shown on the screen. The learner types the answer.
tips: The maths is easy on purpose. The point is the English: plus, equals, and the number words.
Teach the other ways to say it too: four and three, four add three.
Next, play [Add the Money](add-the-money) for the same sums with dollars.

games.name: Add the Money
games.seo: Add the Money: Add Two Amounts in Dollars | Free Money Maths for Adult English Learners
games.meta: Hear "What is five dollars plus three dollars?" and type the total. Free money and numeracy game for adults.
games.sub: Add two amounts of money.
games.blurb: Add two amounts in whole dollars, like $5 and $3. The question is spoken and shown, like working out a total at the shops.
games.about: Adding two amounts of money in whole dollars. The question is spoken and shown, like "$5 + $3 = ?". It practises the word "dollars" and working out a total when shopping.
games.cls: Choose Add the Money in the Teacher Game, then follow with Shop.
inside: Two whole dollar amounts that add up to $10 or less, like $5 + $3.
The question is spoken, What is five dollars plus three dollars?, and shown on the screen. The learner types the total.
tips: Use a shopping list on the board: milk $3, bread $4. How much altogether?
Teach how much altogether and total, the words used at the checkout.
Next, play [Shop](shop) to pay with coins and notes.

games.name: Put In Order
games.seo: Put In Order: Order Numbers, Australian Money, Days and Months | Free Game for Adults
games.meta: Drag numbers, coins and notes, days or months into order. Free ordering and sequencing game for adult English learners.
games.sub: Put numbers, money, days and months in order.
games.blurb: Put numbers, Australian coins and notes, three days or three months in order. Tap or drag the tiles.
games.about: An ordering game with four kinds of rounds: numbers from smallest to biggest, Australian coins and notes from smallest to biggest, three days of the week in order, and three months in order.
how: Tap or drag them into order.
games.cls: Choose Put In Order in the Teacher Game.
inside: Four kinds of round, mixed: numbers, money, days and months.
Numbers: three numbers between 1 and 100, from smallest to biggest.
Money: three Australian coins or notes, from 5c to $50, from smallest to biggest.
Days and months: three in a row, like Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, to put in order.
tips: Coins can be tricky: the $2 coin is smaller than the $1 coin, and the 50c coin is the biggest. Put real coins in order on the table.
Ask learners to say the order aloud as they tap: smallest, then bigger, then biggest.
For more on days and months, play [Days of the Week](days) and [Months](months).

games.name: Tens and Ones
games.seo: Tens and Ones: Place Value Game for Adult Learners | Free Numeracy in English
games.meta: How many tens in 47? How many ones? Free place value game for adult numeracy and English learners.
games.sub: How many tens and how many ones.
games.blurb: See a number from 11 to 99 and answer how many tens or how many ones. Every question is read aloud and shown on screen.
games.about: A place value game for the numbers 11 to 99. The learner sees a number and answers "How many tens?" or "How many ones?". The question is spoken as well as shown.
games.cls: Choose Tens and Ones in the Teacher Game.
inside: Numbers from 11 to 99.
Each round asks How many tens in 47? or How many ones in 47?, spoken and shown.
The wrong choices include the other digit of the same number, so the learner has to know which place is which.
tips: Use bundles of ten, like pop sticks or $10 notes and $1 coins, so learners can see the tens and ones.
Link it to money: 47 dollars is four $10 notes and seven $1 coins.
Practise saying the numbers with [Numbers 21 to 99](numbers-21-99).

games.name: Read the List
games.seo: Read the List: Find Prices on a Price List | Free Shopping English for Adults
games.meta: Read a short price list, find how much something costs, and spot the cheaper item. Free reading and numeracy for adults.
games.sub: Find a price in a list.
games.blurb: Read a price list for everyday groceries and answer how much, which is cheaper, or which is more expensive.
games.about: A price list reading game, like a menu or a shop board. Rounds ask "How much is the bread?", "Which one is cheaper?" or "Which one is more expensive?". The items are everyday groceries at believable prices.
games.cls: Choose Read the List in the Teacher Game.
inside: A short price list of groceries like bread, milk, eggs, apples, cheese, rice, tea, coffee, bananas and soap.
Two kinds of round, taking turns: find a price in a list of four, and compare two prices.
Prices are whole dollars up to $10.
The questions are How much is the bread?, Which one is cheaper? and Which one is more expensive?
tips: Bring in a real price list, like a café menu or a supermarket catalogue, and ask the same questions.
Cheaper and more expensive are the words to teach first. Most and least can come later.
For paying the price, play [Shop](shop).

games.name: Find the Date
games.seo: Find the Date: Read a Calendar in English | Free Calendar Game for Adult Learners
games.meta: Read a month calendar: what day is May 14? Which month is this? Free calendar reading practice for adults.
games.sub: Find a day and a date on a calendar.
games.blurb: Read a real month calendar to find what day a date falls on, or which month it shows. Practice for appointments and due dates.
games.about: Calendar reading with a real month grid. The learner answers "What day is May 14?" by finding the date and reading its column, or answers "Which month is this?". It is practice for appointments, rent and school dates.
games.cls: Choose Find the Date in the Teacher Game. The calendar shows big on the projector.
inside: A real month calendar, with the days of the week across the top. Any of the twelve months can come up.
Two kinds of question: What day is May 14?, and Which month is this?
The four choices can be heard as well as read.
tips: Use the class calendar or a learner's appointment card and ask the same question about real dates.
Show how to read down a column to find the day, and across the top to find its name.
For saying dates aloud, play [Ordinal Numbers](ordinal-numbers).

games.name: First, Second, Third
games.seo: First, Second, Third: Ordinal Numbers Game | Free English for Adult Learners
games.meta: Hear "Tap second" or "Tap the second one", or say which one is marked. Free ordinal numbers game for adult English learners.
games.sub: Which one is first, second or third.
games.blurb: Hear first, second or third and tap the right person in a row, or name a marked position. The words for queues and floors.
games.about: Ordinal numbers with a row of people. The learner hears "Tap second." and chooses 2nd, hears "Tap the second one." and taps the second of 1, 2 and 3, or sees one person marked and names the position. These are the words for queues, floors and dates.
games.cls: Choose First, Second, Third in the Teacher Game, then line up the class for real.
inside: The ordinal words first, second and third.
Three kinds of round: hear Tap second and choose 2nd, hear Tap the second one and tap it in a row, or see one person marked in a row and choose the word.
tips: Line up three learners at the front and ask who is first, second and third.
Use real places where these words come up: the second floor, the first door on the left.
Next, play [Ordinal Numbers](ordinal-numbers) for first to thirtieth.

games.name: Ordinal Numbers
games.seo: Ordinal Numbers 1st to 30th: Listening Game | Free English for Adult Learners
games.meta: Hear "Tap twenty-first" and choose 21st, or find the marked number and name it. Free game for ordinal numbers first to thirtieth.
games.sub: First to thirtieth.
games.blurb: Ordinals from first to thirtieth, the way dates are said. The wrong choices are the usual mix-ups, like thirteenth and thirtieth.
games.about: Ordinal numbers from first to thirtieth, the way dates are said. The learner hears "Tap twelfth." and chooses 12th, hears "Tap the twelfth one." and taps 12 from numbers in counting order, or sees one number marked on a grid of 1 to 30 and chooses its word. The wrong options are the ones people mix up: thirteenth and thirtieth, twelfth and twentieth.
games.cls: Choose Ordinal Numbers in the Teacher Game, then say the dates of this month's classes aloud.
inside: Ordinal numbers from first to thirtieth, the range used for dates.
Three kinds of round: hear Tap twelfth and choose 12th, hear Tap the twelfth one and tap it from numbers in counting order, or see one number marked on a grid of 1 to 30 and choose its word.
The wrong choices are the ones people mix up: the numbers either side, the same last digit, and thirteenth against thirtieth.
tips: First, second, third, twenty-first and thirtieth do not follow the th pattern. Practise them on their own.
Say the dates of this month's classes aloud: Monday the third, Monday the tenth.
Follow with [Find the Date](find-the-date).

games.name: Where Is It
games.seo: Where Is It: Up, Down, Left, Right, In Front, Behind | Free English Game for Adults
games.meta: Position words game: which way does the arrow point? Where is the box? Free prepositions of place for adult learners.
games.sub: Up, down, left, right, in front, behind.
games.blurb: Say which way an arrow points, up, down, left or right, or whether a box is in front of or behind a person.
games.about: Direction and position words. The learner sees an arrow and answers which way it points (up, down, left or right), or sees a person and a box and answers whether the box is in front or behind.
games.cls: Choose Where Is It in the Teacher Game.
inside: Six words: up, down, left, right, in front and behind.
Arrow rounds ask which way the arrow points. Picture rounds show a person and a box, and ask whether the box is in front or behind.
The four choices can be heard as well as read.
tips: Play it standing up: point left, point right, then put a bag in front of you and behind you.
Left and right are hard for many adults in any language. Use a mark on the left hand as a reminder.
Next, use these words on a map with [Directions](directions).

games.name: Clock
games.seo: Interactive Clock Game: Move the Hour and Minute Hands | Free Telling Time for Adults
games.meta: Drag the clock hands to set the time, and read analogue clocks. O'clock, half past, quarter past, quarter to, 5 minutes. Free.
games.sub: Read the clock and set the time.
games.blurb: Read an analogue clock, then drag its hands to set a time. It moves from o'clock and half past to quarter past, quarter to and 5-minute steps.
games.about: An interactive analogue clock with hour and minute hands you can drag. Rounds take turns: read the clock and choose the time, then set the clock to a time, like "Set the clock to 3:15, quarter past three". It moves from o'clock to half past, then quarter past and quarter to, then 5-minute steps. The wrong choices are the real mistakes, like reading the hands the wrong way round.
how: Read the clock and tap the time.
Drag the hour and minute hands to the time shown.
games.cls: Choose Clock in the Teacher Game. The clock shows big on the projector and every student sets the hands on their own phone.
inside: An analogue clock with an hour hand and a minute hand.
Two kinds of round, taking turns: read the clock and choose the time, and drag the hands to set a time.
The game moves up in steps: o'clock, then half past, then quarter past and quarter to, then five-minute steps.
The wrong choices are real mistakes, like reading the hands the wrong way round or being an hour out.
tips: Times are said the analogue way here: half past seven, quarter to three. Teach both ways of saying a time.
The short hand is the hour, the long hand is the minutes. Use a real clock in the room.
For the times on phones and appointment cards, play [Digital Time](digital-time).

games.name: Digital Time
games.seo: Digital Time: Hear a Time and Read It in Numbers | Free Telling Time for Adults
games.meta: Hear "nine thirty" and tap 9:30, or type it. Whole hours, quarter hours, AM and PM. Free digital time game for adults.
games.sub: Hear a time and read it in numbers.
games.blurb: Hear a time and tap or type it in numbers, as on a phone or appointment card. Includes quarter hours and the difference between AM and PM.
games.about: Digital time, as on phones, tickets and appointment cards. The learner hears a time and taps the matching digital time, or types it in numbers. It includes whole hours, quarter hours and AM and PM.
how: Tap the matching time, or type it.
games.cls: Choose Digital Time in the Teacher Game.
inside: Two kinds of round, taking turns.
Whole hours, like 7:00: the learner hears the time and taps the clock that shows it.
Times on the hour or quarter hour with AM or PM, like 7:15 AM: the learner hears seven fifteen in the morning and types the time.
Times are said the digital way, seven fifteen, not quarter past seven.
tips: Bring in real appointment cards, bus timetables or a phone screen, and read the times aloud.
AM is the morning and PM is the afternoon and evening. Link them to daily routine: I wake up at 7 AM.
For reading an analogue clock, play [Clock](clock).

games.name: Shop
games.seo: Shop: Pay With Australian Coins and Notes, Work Out Change | Free Money Game for Adults
games.meta: Tap real Australian coins and notes to pay a price, then work out the change. Free money game for adult English learners.
games.sub: Count the coins and pay the right amount.
games.blurb: Pay for everyday items with real Australian coins and notes, from 5c to $50, and work out the change.
games.about: A money game with pictures of real Australian coins and notes, from 5c to $50. The learner pays the right amount for an everyday item at a believable price. Other rounds ask for the change: "It costs $34.50. You give $50.00. Tap your change."
how: Tap coins and notes to pay.
games.cls: Choose Shop in the Teacher Game. Every student pays on their phone and the projector shows who got it right.
inside: Pictures of real Australian coins and notes, from 5c to $50, to tap and pay with.
Two kinds of round, taking turns: pay the exact price, and work out the change.
Pay rounds use prices from $50 to $99.50, for things like a chair, shoes, a jacket or a bicycle.
Change rounds show what you paid with, a $20, $50 or $100 note, and the learner taps the change.
tips: Bring real coins and notes, or printed ones, and set up a shop in the classroom.
Teach the phrases for paying: How much is it? Here you are. Here is your change.
For smaller amounts, start with [Write the Number](write-the-number) and [Add the Money](add-the-money).

games.name: Dice
games.seo: Dice Game: Roll, Add and Get Closest to the Target | Free Number Game for Adults
games.meta: Roll two dice, add to your score, and stop before you go over the target. Free maths and English game, great for a whole class.
games.sub: Roll two dice and get closest to the target.
games.blurb: Roll two dice, add them to your score and choose to roll again or stop. The aim is to get closest to the target without going over.
games.about: A dice game for adding and deciding. The learner rolls two dice, adds them to their score and types the new score, then chooses to roll again or stop. Going over the target means you are out. You choose the target number, and whether a wrong sum ends your game or gives one more try.
how: Roll the dice and type your new score.
Get closest to the target without going over.
games.cls: Choose Dice in the Teacher Game. The whole class races to the target on the projector and the closest score wins.
inside: Two dice, a running score and a target.
The learner rolls, adds the dice to their score and types the new score, then chooses to roll again or stop.
Going over the target means you are out. The target can be 20, 30, 50, 75 or 100, or your own number.
You choose whether a wrong sum ends the game or gives one more try.
tips: Play it as a class from the Teacher Game, where everyone races to the target on the projector.
Ask learners to say each sum aloud: twelve plus five is seventeen.
Talk about the choice to stop or roll again. It is a natural way to practise more, less and close to.

games.name: Signs
games.seo: Signs Game: No Smoking, Wet Floor, Exit, First Aid | Free Safety Signs for English Learners
games.meta: What does this sign mean? Common safety and public signs in Australia: exit, toilets, wet floor, no entry. Free for adults.
games.sub: Read the signs you see around you.
games.blurb: See a public or safety sign with no words on it, like wet floor or no parking, and tap what it means from four choices.
games.about: Common public and safety signs shown as pictures, without words: no smoking, no parking, do not enter, wet floor, danger, first aid, exit, toilets, wheelchair access, no food or drink, and bus stop. The learner taps what the sign means.
games.cls: Choose Signs in the Teacher Game, then walk around the building and find the same signs.
inside: 11 signs shown as pictures with no words: no smoking, no parking, do not enter, wet floor, danger, first aid, exit, toilets, wheelchair access, no food or drink, and bus stop.
The learner reads four meanings and taps the right one.
The wrong meanings are close on purpose, like No cooking and No matches beside No smoking, so the learner has to read carefully.
tips: Walk around your building after the game and find the same signs on the walls.
Teach the pattern No plus a word: no smoking, no parking, no food.
Signs with words, like notices, come next in [Read the Notice](read-the-notice).

games.name: Messages
games.seo: Reading Text Messages: Appointment Reminders and SMS | Free English Reading for Adults
games.meta: Read a text message from a doctor, a dentist, a class or family, and answer a question about it. Free reading practice for adults.
games.sub: Read a short message and answer it.
games.blurb: Read real text messages, like an appointment reminder or a shopping request from family, and answer what day, what time, who or what to bring.
games.about: Reading real-life text messages: a medical appointment reminder ("Reply YES to confirm"), a dental reminder, a class start time, or a message from family asking you to buy milk and bread. The learner answers what day, what time, who, or what to bring.
games.cls: Choose Messages in the Teacher Game, then ask what the learner should do next.
inside: Six text messages: a doctor's appointment, an English class, a request from Mum to buy milk and bread, a dental reminder, a class cancelled because the centre is closed, and a rent reminder from a housing office.
Each round shows one message and asks one question, like What time is the appointment?, Which room is the class in? or How much is the rent?
The wrong choices are close to the right one, like 2:13pm beside 2:30pm, or $302 beside $320.
tips: Ask what the learner should do next: reply YES, bring the book, arrive early.
Show real reminder messages from a phone, with personal details removed, and ask the same questions.
Times and prices are where the mistakes happen. Practise reading them aloud with [Digital Time](digital-time).

games.name: Forms
games.seo: Filling In Forms: First Name, Family Name, Date of Birth, Postcode | Free Practice for Adults
games.meta: Put each detail in the right box on a form, and read an ID card. Free form-filling practice for adult English learners.
games.sub: Fill in a form with your details.
games.blurb: Put a person's details into the right boxes on a form, from family name to postcode. Other rounds read the name or number on an ID card.
games.about: Form-filling practice. The learner gets a person's details and puts each one in the right box: first name, family name, date of birth, phone, address, postcode and country of birth. Other rounds show an ID card and ask for the name or the card number.
how: Put each one in its box.
games.cls: Choose Forms in the Teacher Game, then follow up with a real paper enrolment form.
inside: Two kinds of round, taking turns: filling in a form, and reading an ID card.
Form rounds give six people's details, such as Ali Hassan, Mai Nguyen and Fatima Ahmadi, and the learner puts each detail in the right box.
The boxes are first name, family name, date of birth, phone, address, postcode and country of birth.
Card rounds show an ID card and ask the learner to tap the name or the card number.
tips: Family name and surname mean the same thing. Some forms say last name. Teach all three.
Follow up with a real paper enrolment form, filled in with each learner's own details.
For writing names correctly, play [Copy It](copy-it) and [Big and Small Letters](big-and-small-letters).

games.name: Directions
games.seo: Directions Game: Go Straight Ahead, Turn Left, Next To, Opposite | Free English Map Game for Adults
games.meta: Read or hear directions and draw the way on a street map. Turn left, turn right, next to, opposite, between. Free for adult learners.
games.sub: Read the directions. Draw the way on the map.
games.blurb: Hear and read directions like Turn left at the bank, then draw the way on a street map. Words like next to and opposite find the place.
games.about: Giving and following directions on a street map. The learner hears and reads directions such as "Go straight ahead. Turn left at the bank. The post office is next to the café." and draws the way with a finger, from You are here to the building the sentence describes. The place they are looking for has no name on the map, so the place words (next to, opposite, between, on the corner) are what find it. Directions start short and get longer through the game.
how: Draw the way to the place.
games.cls: Choose Directions in the Teacher Game. The map goes on the projector, and the answer screen shows who found the place, who went another way and who stopped at the wrong building.
inside: A street map with 15 kinds of place, such as a bank, school, park, café, library, chemist, post office, bus stop and train station.
The learner hears and reads directions, then draws the way with a finger from You are here.
The place being looked for has no name on the map. Place words like next to, opposite, between and on the corner are what find it.
Directions start short and get longer through the game.
The right place reached by another way, or the right street but the wrong building, scores part marks.
tips: Teach turn left, turn right and go straight ahead with gestures before playing.
Practise the place words with real buildings near your centre: the chemist is next to the bank.
Learn the position words first with [Where Is It](where-is-it).

games.name: Devices
games.seo: Devices Game: Phone, Laptop, Printer, Charger | Free Digital Skills English for Adults
games.meta: Name a device, or choose which one you use to call, print, type or take a photo. Free digital literacy for adults.
games.sub: Name a device and say what it is for.
games.blurb: Name everyday devices like a printer, charger or headphones, and say what each one is for.
games.about: Digital literacy vocabulary: phone, laptop, screen, printer, camera, keyboard, mouse, headphones, charger and wifi. Rounds ask "What is this called?" or "Which one do you use to print on paper?".
games.cls: Choose Devices in the Teacher Game.
inside: Ten things: phone, laptop, screen, printer, camera, keyboard, mouse, headphones, charger and wifi.
Two kinds of round, taking turns: What is this called?, and Which one do you use to call someone, print on paper, take a photo, type, point and click, listen, or give it power?
The charger is drawn as the small block and cable that comes with a phone, not a wall plug.
tips: Point to the real devices in the room, or on learners' own phones: the camera, the charger, the headphones.
Many of these words are the same in other languages, like laptop and wifi. Ask learners which ones they already know.
Next, play [Screen Symbols](screen-symbols) for the icons on a screen.

games.name: Screen Symbols
