games.seo: Screen Symbols: What Phone and Computer Icons Mean | Free Digital Literacy for Adults
games.meta: Search, home, back, play, pause, sound off, wifi, battery, settings, delete, save, menu. Learn what screen icons mean. Free.
games.sub: What the buttons on a screen do.
games.blurb: See an icon, like search, settings, back or delete, and tap its name. The symbols on phones, computers and kiosks.
games.about: The icons on phones, computers and kiosks: search, home, go back, play, pause, sound on, sound off, internet, battery, settings, delete, save, camera, message and menu. The learner sees the icon and taps its name.
games.cls: Choose Screen Symbols in the Teacher Game, then find the same icons on students' own phones.
good: digital literacy for seniors and migrants
inside: 15 symbols: search, home, go back, play, pause, sound on, sound off, internet, battery, settings, delete, save, camera, message and menu.
Each round shows one symbol and asks What is this?. The learner taps its name from four.
tips: Ask learners to find the same symbols on their own phones after the game.
The menu symbol, three short lines, is the one most learners do not know. Show where it opens on a real app.
Next, play [What Should You Do?](what-should-you-do) to act on what the phone shows.

games.name: What Should You Do?
games.seo: What Should You Do? Phone Messages, Battery Low, Scam Calls | Free Digital Skills for Adults
games.meta: Battery low, no internet, wrong password, missed call. Read the phone message and choose what to do. Free.
games.sub: A message, or a problem with the phone.
games.blurb: Choose what to do about a phone message, like battery low, storage full or a missed call. Also what to check when the phone will not turn on.
games.about: Common phone messages and what to do about them: battery low, no internet, storage full, wrong password, a missed call, a new message, someone calling, a locked phone and an alarm. Other rounds ask what to check or tap when the phone will not turn on or nothing will load.
games.cls: Choose What Should You Do? in the Teacher Game, then try the same things on students' own phones.
inside: Ten phone messages: battery low, no internet, delete this photo?, storage full, wrong password, missed call, new message, someone is calling, phone locked, and an alarm.
For each one the learner chooses what to do, like Charge it, Turn on wifi, Cancel or Call back.
Six more rounds are about fixing a problem, like It will not turn on. What do you check? The answers are pictures, such as a battery or a charger.
tips: Do the same things for real on a learner's phone, like turning the sound off at the start of class.
Talk about Cancel. Many learners tap the first button on a message without reading it.
For staying safe online, play [Security](safe-or-private).

games.name: Security
games.seo: Security: What Not to Share Online | Free Scam Awareness and Digital Safety for Adults
games.meta: Can you share your PIN? Your first name? Learn what to keep private, and copy a verification code. Free.
games.sub: Copy a code, and what to keep private.
games.blurb: Decide if something is safe to share, like a first name, or must stay private, like a PIN or passport photo. Other rounds copy a 4-digit SMS code.
games.about: Online safety with yes or no answers. The learner decides whether something is safe to share, like a first name, a class day or a favourite colour, or must stay private, like a bank PIN, a password, a card number or a photo of a passport. Other rounds practise copying a 4-digit code, like a verification code sent by SMS.
how: Decide if you can share it.
Tap yes or no, or type the code.
games.cls: Choose Security in the Teacher Game, then talk about scams before setting up banking or myGov apps.
inside: Two kinds of round, taking turns: can you share this?, and copy a code.

The share rounds name one thing with a picture, and the learner taps yes or no. Keep private: bank PIN, password, bank card number and a photo of your passport. Safe to share: first name, class day, teacher's name and favourite colour.
The code rounds show a 4-digit code, like the one a bank or myGov sends by text, and the learner types it.
tips: Talk about scams: a bank or the government will never ask for your PIN or password by text or phone.
Use it before helping learners set up banking or myGov on their phones.
Practise reading codes and numbers aloud with [Tap the Number](tap-the-number).

games.name: All Games
games.seo: All English Games Mixed: Letters, Words, Numbers, Time, Money | Free Practice for Adults
games.meta: A mix of every WordLink game in one round. Free English practice for adult learners. No sign-up.
games.sub: A mix of every game.
games.blurb: One mixed round drawn from every game. A quick review across all skills.
games.about: One round drawn from every game: letters and sounds, reading, writing, vocabulary, listening, speaking, grammar, numbers, time, money, everyday English and digital skills.
games.cls: Choose All Games in the Teacher Game for a mixed review quiz.
inside: Questions drawn from every game, across letters and sounds, reading, writing, vocabulary, listening, speaking, grammar, numbers, everyday English and using a device.
You choose how many questions. It does not get harder or easier as you go.
tips: Use it as a short warm-up or end-of-lesson review once learners know several games.
A mixed round is a good way to remind learners of games they have not played for a while.
For a check that adjusts to each learner, use [Test Yourself](test-yourself) instead.

games.name: Test Yourself
games.seo: Test Yourself: Free Adaptive English Test for Adult Learners | WordLink
games.meta: 10 rounds of 3 questions from every game. It gets harder or easier as you go, and shows what to practise next.
games.sub: 10 rounds of 3 questions, drawn from every game. It gets harder or easier as you go.
games.blurb: Ten rounds from every game that get harder or easier with each answer. The results show strong skills and which games to practise next.
games.about: An adaptive self-check. The questions get harder after right answers and easier after wrong ones. At the end the learner sees their strong skills and which games to practise next.
how: The test changes to match you.
games.cls: Test Yourself is played on each student's own phone, and the results tell the teacher who needs what. For a whole-class check, run the Level Check from the Teacher Game.
good: free English level test for adults
inside: Questions from every skill in WordLink, from tapping a letter up to writing a missing word in a longer sentence.
Ten rounds of three questions. After a perfect round the test moves up two steps, and after a round the learner cannot do it moves down two.
At the end the learner sees their strong skills and which games to practise next.
tips: Learners can take it on their own phones in a few minutes, at the start of a course and again later to see progress.
It is a self-check for the learner. For a placement result with an ACSF level, use the [Level Check](level-check).
To check one skill only, use the skill tests, like [Test Yourself: Reading](test-reading).

games.name: Test Yourself: Letters and Sounds
games.seo: Letters and Sounds Test: Free Adaptive Phonics Check for Adult Learners | WordLink
games.meta: 10 rounds of 3 questions from every letters and sounds game: letter names, big and small letters, word families and digraphs.
games.sub: 10 rounds of 3 questions, drawn from every letters and sounds game. It gets harder or easier as you go.
games.blurb: An adaptive check of the alphabet and all six phonics games. The results point to the phonics games to practise next.
games.about: An adaptive check of letters and phonics. It draws on Letter Names, Big and Small Letters and all six Sound Gap, Tap Word and Build Word games, from CVC word families up to digraphs and vowel teams.
how: The test changes to match you.
games.cls: Students take it on their own phones. The results show which phonics games each one should practise next.
inside: Nine steps, easiest first: hear a letter, match big and small letters, the three Beginner sound games, write a name with a capital, then the three Elementary sound games.
Ten rounds of three questions. After a perfect round the test moves up two steps, and after a round the learner cannot do it moves down two.
At the end the learner sees the step they reached, and that game is offered to practise next.
tips: Use it in the first week to see who needs the alphabet and who is ready for phonics.
The step a learner reaches points straight to the game to practise, like [Beginner Build Word](beginner-build-word).

games.name: Test Yourself: Vocabulary
games.seo: English Vocabulary Test: Free Adaptive Word Check for Adult Learners | WordLink
games.meta: 10 rounds of 3 questions from every vocabulary game: days, months, weather, fruit, body, clothes, devices and more.
games.sub: 10 rounds of 3 questions, drawn from every vocabulary game. It gets harder or easier as you go.
games.blurb: An adaptive check across every vocabulary topic, plus sight words, devices and question words.
games.about: An adaptive vocabulary check. It draws on Days of the Week, Months, Weather, Fruits, Parts of the Body, Clothes, Question Words, Sight Words, Picture and Word, Devices, All Spelling, Odd One Out and Translate.
how: The test changes to match you.
games.cls: Students take it on their own phones. It shows which topics each one already knows.
inside: 18 steps, from tapping the word for a picture and finding the odd one out, through fruit, the body, devices, clothes, days and months, up to spelling words and translating.
Tapping a word comes before writing the same word, so a topic can appear twice.
Ten rounds of three questions. After a perfect round the test moves up two steps, and after a round the learner cannot do it moves down two.
tips: Use it to see which topics a learner already knows, so class time goes on the ones they do not.
The single topic games, like [Fruits](fruits) and [Clothes](clothes), give practice on the gaps it finds.

games.name: Test Yourself: Listening
games.seo: English Listening Test: Free Adaptive Listening Check for Adult Learners | WordLink
games.meta: 10 rounds of 3 questions from every listening game: greetings, instructions, gap-fill sentences and more.
games.sub: 10 rounds of 3 questions, drawn from every listening game. It gets harder or easier as you go.
games.blurb: An adaptive check of how well a learner understands spoken letters, words, sentences, times and instructions.
games.about: An adaptive listening check: how well the learner understands spoken letters, words, sentences, times, greetings and instructions. It draws on the listening gap-fill games, Listen and Unscramble, the Speaking Game, Greetings, Do What It Says, Letter Names, the phonics games, Digital Time, First, Second, Third and Where Is It.
how: The test changes to match you.
games.cls: Students take it on their own phones, with headphones in a busy room.
inside: 18 steps, from hearing a letter and replying to a greeting, through times, instructions and the sound games, up to writing a missing word and building an answer to a spoken question.
Ten rounds of three questions. After a perfect round the test moves up two steps, and after a round the learner cannot do it moves down two.
At the end the learner sees the step they reached, and that game is offered to practise next.
tips: In a busy room, ask learners to use headphones.
For gaps it finds, the listening gap games are a good next step: [Beginner Listen and Fill Gaps](beginner-listening).

games.name: Test Yourself: Speaking
games.seo: English Speaking Preparation Test: Free Adaptive Check for Adult Learners | WordLink
games.meta: 10 rounds of 3 questions from the speaking games: everyday questions, question words, greetings and word order.
games.sub: 10 rounds of 3 questions, drawn from every speaking game. It gets harder or easier as you go.
games.blurb: An adaptive check of the language behind speaking: answering questions, choosing question words, replying to greetings and ordering a sentence.
games.about: An adaptive check of the language learners need to speak: answering everyday questions, choosing question words, replying to greetings and putting a sentence in order. It draws on the Speaking Game, Question Words, Listen and Unscramble and Greetings.
